claims.text: The as-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has poor mechanical integrity and tends to crack under applied-field and pressure-field operation.
The as-cast alloy has a large caloric response.
The as-cast alloy has compressive strength notably below 152 MPa.
Annealing at approximately 500°C for 1 hour under an inert atmosphere followed by rapid quenching will induce nanoscale coherent precipitates.
The induced precipitates will be coherent intermetallic phases, such as Mn-rich or Ni-rich phases.
The precipitates will form both along grain boundaries and within grains.
The precipitates will impede crack initiation and propagation by pinning grain boundaries.
Optimized precipitate size and volume fraction will not hinder the intrinsic magneto-structural transition responsible for the caloric effect.
The aging treatment will significantly improve the alloy's mechanical integrity relative to the as-cast state.
The aged alloy will attain compressive strength exceeding 250 MPa.
The aged alloy will retain a caloric response comparable in magnitude to that of the untreated alloy.
The proposed benefit applies under magnetic fields, pressure, and temperatures near the alloy's caloric transition.
Aging temperature and time must be tightly controlled to prevent precipitate over-stabilization from suppressing the caloric transition.
Departures from optimal aging parameters may shift or dampen the caloric response.
TEM can be used to test whether the proposed coherent nanoscale precipitates form and to measure their distribution.
The hypothesis is falsified if aging fails to produce a statistically significant compressive-strength increase, with a target above 250 MPa, relative to the as-cast control.
The hypothesis is falsified if aging significantly diminishes caloric entropy change or adversely changes the transition temperature relative to the untreated control.
